items.candidate: Use valid group-sequential stopping with practical margins/precision targets.
items.mechanism: Pre-specify sequential looks, alpha spending and effect/futility or precision thresholds; use full data for near-ties.
items.uncertainty: Independence/normality and multiple-comparison assumptions need clustered long-horizon extensions; margins are user-chosen.
items.tested_scope: 206 VLMs/31 multimodal benchmarks under sample-level sequential assumptions.
items.quantitative_result: ~15%/30%/50% samples for ±3/±2/±1.5pp widths; fixed 1.2K resolves 55% of 1,000 pairs vs 76% sequentially; >2pp gaps often save ≥60%.
items.why_new_relative_to_O: No valid group-sequential alpha-spending evaluation rule with practical margins was found in O.

items.candidate: Audit benchmark task validity/composition and ranking sensitivity.
items.mechanism: Pin audited task manifests and compare rankings on the same stored trajectories before/after validity filtering; separate repaired-task reruns.
items.uncertainty: Filtering is not proof every dropped task is invalid; repaired-task reruns and partial-coverage rows are separate issues.
items.tested_scope: AgentSuite ICML 2026 committed trajectories and audit-filter splits.
items.quantitative_result: τ-bench top two reverse; ACEBench Kimi-K2 vs Gemini-2.5-Pro reverses; overall Kimi rank 2→3 and o3-high 3→2, with no new trajectories.
items.why_new_relative_to_O: O has evidence/provenance controls but no same-trajectory benchmark-composition ranking-sensitivity audit.

items.candidate: Treat message-role/authority representation as a controlled factor in self-correction.
items.mechanism: Hold an erroneous claim byte-identical while varying self/user/tool/memory role, then score explicit correction and final action separately.
items.uncertainty: Measures explicit error flagging, not guaranteed final-answer improvement; errors are pre-localized and external-role trust can be unsafe.
items.tested_scope: 13 model-domain cells, seven model families, three domains, n=30 paired tasks/cell.
items.quantitative_result: External-role relabeling raises explicit correction by 23–93pp; Llama-3.3-70B generated logic 0% baseline to +93.3pp under neutral user-role relabeling.
items.why_new_relative_to_O: No message-role relabeling self-correction experiment or role-conditioned error-addressability mechanism was found in O.

items.candidate: Evaluate a failure monitor together with its intervention, not by detector accuracy alone.
items.mechanism: Measure failure prevalence p, recovery r and disruption d under intervention; use p*r-(1-p)*d and final outcomes.
items.uncertainty: Model/benchmark/threshold/intervention specific; high AUROC is not itself harmful and p/r/d is deployment-specific.
items.tested_scope: HotPotQA, GAIA and ALFWorld failure-monitor interventions across three agents.
items.quantitative_result: Critic AUROC .936/F1 .963, yet intervention deltas include HotPotQA -2.3/0/-25.5pp and GAIA -4.4/-4.4/-30.0pp; ALFWorld only +0.5 to +2.8pp.
items.why_new_relative_to_O: O has outcome/regression controls but no explicit p/r/d operating curve for learned failure monitors.

items.candidate: Measure error correlation/effective independent vote count before treating judge panels as multiple evidence channels.
items.mechanism: Estimate held-out error correlation/effective sample size and prefer genuinely independent evidence when nominal panel size overstates effective votes.
items.uncertainty: Classification/preference evaluation differs from open-ended O candidate evaluation; n_eff thresholds are heuristic.
items.tested_scope: Nine judges on 1,000 ChaosNLI-MNLI items plus RewardBench; chain-of-thought decorrelation also tested.
items.quantitative_result: Nine nominal judges n_eff=2.18 [2.07,2.31], mean error correlation .391±.111; RewardBench n_eff=1.99 and best single 95.5% vs panel 92.7%.
items.why_new_relative_to_O: No LLM judge panel, error-correlation estimator or effective-vote budgeting mechanism was found in O.

items.candidate: Require persistent self-improvement to beat matched test-time discovery and show reuse on disjoint tasks.
items.mechanism: Compare persistent updates against equal-budget direct/parallel/sequential search, then test disjoint transfer with a safe base fallback.
items.uncertainty: One Terminal-Bench 2.1 study/two-run averages does not reject harness evolution generally; value is task/scaffold dependent.
items.tested_scope: Terminal-Bench 2.1, common initial harness, K=5 matched compute, with/without unit tests, plus 45/10/34 disjoint split.
items.quantitative_result: Without tests direct/parallel/sequential/evolution 68.2/72.3/69.3/67.4; with tests 72.9/86.0/84.3/75.8. Disjoint initial 67.7 vs evolved 68.3 (+0.6).
items.why_new_relative_to_O: O has protected baselines/held-out gates but has not shown a persistent harness update beats matched test-time search and transfers on this disjoint control.

candidate_gate.admission_rule: complete traceable novelty + evidence-strength + decision-relevance triplet; current-wave high-information-density/nonredundancy curation, not exhaustive promotion
candidate_gate.curation_note: Revision 6 intentionally refreshes the compact feed to six strongest nonredundant current-wave additions. All revision-5 feed candidates remain preserved in the clean index/history; omission is not rejection or negative evidence.
